The Amount Input guide and its evidence were checked on 22 September 2026 on jfs-components 0.1.60 (its Sources note still says so); the installed package is 0.1.78 (mirror v0.1.78-dbe0e02). Read against the installed AmountInput.tsx, MoneyValue.tsx and NoteInput.tsx, with their tokens through the package's resolver, every sentence this entry quotes still holds, but two NoteInput sentences are out of date. The Sources note's “The NoteInput state prop is accepted but unused by the implementation; its visible editing state is focus-driven.” is contradicted: NoteInput reads state, and state Editing hides the placeholder as focus does (NoteInput.tsx lines 50, 68–69, 170 and 177). The States description's “NoteInput responds to focus and controlled text; its internal state is runtime-driven.” says less than the package: a note with no value keeps what people type on its own and still calls onChangeText (NoteInput.tsx lines 55–57 and 148–151), as the NoteInput guide now says. Both changed between the 8 October (v0.1.78-636f3f5) and 12 October (v0.1.78-c1fa197) builds; AmountInput.tsx itself is the same blob from v0.1.78 to dbe0e02. The entry doesn't quote either sentence. Re-check the guide on 0.1.78 and publish it, then re-extract. Added by Claude Code in the overnight run agentpack-batch13, for Marcin to confirm. Guide fix #536.

summary: Make monetary entry primary while keeping optional detail close.

anatomy.holds: The currency symbol gives the amount a clear unit. It is the currency of the MoneyValue in the amount slot (₹ by default), drawn before the amount; an empty currency leaves the amount without a unit, which the Do & Don'ts rule out.

examples.purpose: A transfer review, the guide's In context: a Card titled for the task gives the entry its context, the AmountInput keeps the amount primary with an editable ₹500 and a note under it, so the person knows what they are completing. AmountInput carries Context3 Amount Input, as the guide's own source sets it, because it doesn't set its own context and passes its modes to both children; the children carry none. The literal amount and the empty onValueChange stand for the screen's own state (MoneyValue shows the value it is given); the note keeps what people type and onChangeText gives the screen each change.
examples.jsx:
<Card>
  <Card.Title>Review transfer</Card.Title>
  <Card.SupportText>Enter the amount and an optional note before sending.</Card.SupportText>
  <AmountInput
    modes={{ Context3: 'Amount Input' }}
    moneyValueSlot={<MoneyValue value="500" currency="₹" editable onValueChange={(amount) => {}} />}
    noteInputSlot={<NoteInput placeholder="Add transfer note" onChangeText={(note) => {}} />}
  />
</Card>

from.quote: A Card gives the entry a task context while AmountInput keeps amount primary.
